title: Discrete weights and spaces of coherent cocones
statement:
Use universes, nerves, quasicategories, coherent functors, transformations and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the space category $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Let $A$ be a $\mathcal V$-small ordinary category, $W:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Set}_{\mathcal V}$ an ordinary presheaf, and view $W$ also as a coherent presheaf of discrete spaces. Define its category of elements $E_W$ to have objects $(a,w)$ with $w\in W(a)$ and arrows $(a,w)\to(a',w')$ the arrows $r:a\to a'$ satisfying $w=W(r)(w')$; composition is composition in $A$. Write $\pi:E_W\to A$ for projection. Let $\mathcal C$ be a $\mathcal V$-small quasicategory, $F:N(A)\to\mathcal C$ a coherent functor, and $z\in\mathcal C$. The coherent Hom bifunctor of [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] defines $Q_{F,z}:N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ by $Q_{F,z}(a)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(F(a),z)$. There is a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(A)^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})}(W,Q_{F,z})\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(E_W),\mathcal C)}(F N(\pi),\Delta_{N(E_W)}z).$$
It sends a transformation $t$ to the coherent cocone whose leg at $(a,w)$ is $t_a(w):F(a)\to z$, retaining all naturality and higher homotopies. This equivalence is natural in $F,z$ and in maps of ordinary presheaves: a map $W\to W'$ induces $E_W\to E_{W'}$, and precomposition on the left corresponds to restriction of cocones on the right. No colimits in $\mathcal C$ are assumed; empty weights and empty categories are allowed. All functor categories are formed in containing universes.

source.place: Agent-formulated discrete-weight cocone calculation in the Yoneda proof of Proposition 6.4.9, printed p.298, using Corollary 6.2.16 (p.281, category-of-elements density), Corollary 6.3.5 and its dual (pp.288-289, representable mapping-space calculation), and the coherent Yoneda lemma. The equivalence of weighted transformations with coherent cocones, including its evaluation map, is stated explicitly here rather than attributed verbatim to 6.4.9. Online source read; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this assertion.

proof.text: Put $B=N(A)$, $K=N(E_W)$ and $p=N(\pi)$. These are $\mathcal V$-small: their simplices are finite strings in small sets. An ordinary nerve is a quasicategory: an inner 2-horn is filled by composition, and in higher dimensions the composable string determines the simplex, with its required faces by associativity. We verify directly that $p$ is a right fibration, using [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Over a chain $a_0\to\cdots\to a_n$, a simplex of $K$ is uniquely determined by its last element $w_n$, setting $w_j=W(a_j\to a_n)(w_n)$. A right horn $\Lambda_i^n$ with $i>0$ includes the last vertex. For $n=1$ that vertex determines its filler. For $n=2,i=1$, the horn gives the edges $0\to1\to2$, whose equations imply the formula for $w_0,w_1$; for $i=2$ it gives $0\to2$ and $1\to2$, giving those formulas directly. For $n\geq3$, each edge $j\to n$ belongs to some face other than the omitted face, so the horn again forces these formulas. Each supplied face is the unique lift of its base string with its given last element; the formula therefore restricts to every supplied face and is a filler. The formula commutes with faces and degeneracies. Transport along $r:a\to a'$ with target $w'$ has the unique source $W(r)(w')$; uniqueness of these lifted strings gives exactly the strict functor's higher composition data. For $\eta:W\to W'$, naturality gives the map over $A$ sending $(a,w)$ to $(a,\eta_a(w))$, and hence the specified map of nerves.

source.place: Paragraph 2, elementary category-of-elements horn calculation for the coherent comma-cocone foundation; written out after the relative-nerve citation acquired a cyclic dependency.

proof.text: Use the specific comparison of [lem-coef-cone-straightening-coherent-evaluation]. It identifies enriched evaluation $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathsf D_B^{cf})\to\operatorname{Fun}(B^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$ with the specified ordered-cone adjunction $T\dashv U_B$ and gives an equivalence $\Phi_B:N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathsf{RFib}(B))\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(B^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$. Its natural comparison $\Phi_B(q)\simeq m_q$ is a comparison of whole coherent diagrams, with fibre evaluation and every parameter simplex specified. In particular $\Phi_B(p)\simeq W$: by the unique-lift formula in Step 1 and the definition of $m_q$ in [lem-coef-right-fibration-section-limit], transport for $p$ is exactly $W$, including all higher composition data. We use this cone-compatible equivalence throughout the rest of the proof. No identification of coherent diagrams is inferred merely from their values on vertices.

source.place: Specific cone/evaluation compatibility isolated in lem-coef-cone-straightening-coherent-evaluation, with transport for the discrete fibration calculated directly in Step 1.

proof.text: Let $S_z=\mathcal C_{/z}$ be the join slice and form $q:Y=B\times_{F,\mathcal C}S_z\to B$. By [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] this is a right fibration, whose fibre at $a$ is exactly the right-pinched space $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(F(a),z)$. Apply the concrete-slice compatibility clause of [lem-coef-cone-straightening-coherent-evaluation] with $S=B$, $C=\mathcal C$, $v=F$ and $c=z$. It gives $\Phi_B(q)\simeq H_{\mathcal C}(F(-),z)=Q_{F,z}$ as coherent functors, preserving the underlying edge and all parameter simplices. The equality on the right is the definition of $Q_{F,z}$ in the item using [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality]. Thus the comparison with that specific Hom bifunctor is a cited theorem; agreement on precomposition of edges alone is not used to identify two coherent diagrams. The hypotheses hold because $B$ is a small nerve and hence a quasicategory, and $\mathcal C$ is $\mathcal V$-small. The pullback $Y$ is also $\mathcal V$-small degree by degree.

source.place: Concrete-slice and canonical-Hom compatibility of lem-coef-cone-straightening-coherent-evaluation; join slice from Section 2.1.2.

proof.text:
For completeness, pass from the straightening equivalence to its concrete mapping complexes as follows. If $\mathcal D$ is any locally Kan simplicial category and $x,y$ are its objects, the rigidification/nerve adjunction gives a simplicial identification $\operatorname{Map}^{R}_{N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal D}(x,y)=\operatorname{Sing}_Q(\mathcal D(x,y))$: an $n$-simplex on the left is an enriched functor from $\mathfrak C[(\Delta^n\star\{y\})\amalg_{\Delta^n}\{x\}]$, so its only nonidentity mapping datum is $Q^n\to\mathcal D(x,y)$. This identification respects simplex operators and enriched functors. By [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution], the zigzag $\operatorname{Sing}_Q(T)\leftarrow|\operatorname{Sing}_Q(T)|_Q\to T$ consists of weak equivalences for Kan $T$ (the first map is $p_{\operatorname{Sing}_QT}$ and the second the evaluation counit). Both ends are Kan: the nerve is a quasicategory by [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-quasicategory], and its mapping spaces are Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Apply this directly to the locally Kan simplicial category $\mathsf{RFib}(B)$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. The mapping complex of right fibrations is the Kan complex $\operatorname{Fun}_{/B}(K,Y)$ by [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. Since a functor equivalence induces equivalences on all mapping spaces by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], the equivalence $\Phi_B$ of [lem-coef-cone-straightening-coherent-evaluation] and Steps 1--3 give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})}(W,Q_{F,z})\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{/B}(K,Y).$$
The fibre-evaluation compatibility of that same node identifies restriction of the map of right fibrations with the component of the transformation, including all its simplicial parameters.

source.place: Section 2.2.2 and Proposition 2.2.3.11; coherent-nerve mapping comparison derived explicitly from the pinched resolution, without using the cyclic general coherent-nerve node.

proof.text: Put $G=F p$. By the defining pullback of $Y$, the right side of Step 4 is, in every degree, the space of lifts $K\times\Delta^n\to S_z$ of $G\,\mathrm{pr}_K$. Replace the join slice $S_z\to\mathcal C$ by the target-fixed arrow fibration $T_z=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,\mathcal C}\{z\}\to\mathcal C$. The map $\delta_z:S_z\to T_z$ of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence] is over $\mathcal C$ and is an equivalence; both projections are right fibrations by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] and [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration]. By [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] it is a weak equivalence on each Kan fibre. The fibrewise criterion of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] now gives an inverse and simplicial homotopies over $\mathcal C$. Composing with those maps and homotopies gives an equivalence between the spaces of lifts of $G$ to $S_z$ and to $T_z$, with the entire boundary diagram fixed. This argument uses an inverse over the base, so it justifies the strict-fibre restriction; an arbitrary equivalence of total categories alone would not justify it.

source.place: Arrow-to-join slice comparison (Kerodon 02VT, Construction 02GH); HTT Lemma 2.2.3.6 for the fibrewise inverse over the base.

proof.text:
Currying is a degreewise simplicial isomorphism from the last lift space to the arrow mapping space
$$U_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(G,\Delta_Kz).$$
Indeed an $n$-simplex on either side is exactly a map $K\times\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal C$ whose restriction at the initial interval endpoint is $G\,\mathrm{pr}_K$ and whose restriction at the final endpoint is constant at $z$; permutations of the two parameter factors identify the conventions. Its face and degeneracy maps restrict the same $\Delta^n$ factor. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ is a quasicategory. The natural pinch equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] then identifies this arrow mapping space with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(G,\Delta_Kz)$. Composing with Steps 4--5 proves the displayed equivalence in the statement.

source.place: Internal-functor adjunction and the right-pinch comparison; the currying equality is written out degreewise.

proof.text: Track evaluation through this comparison. By the fibre-evaluation and concrete-slice compatibilities of [lem-coef-cone-straightening-coherent-evaluation], a transformation $t:W\to Q_{F,z}$ gives a map $K\to Y$ over $B$ whose map on the fibre at $a$ is $t_a$. The vertex $(a,w)$ therefore goes to the right-pinched arrow $t_a(w):F(a)\to z$. The map $\delta_z$ sends its $0$-simplex to that same edge, and the pinch comparison also sends a $0$-simplex to its corresponding edge. Hence the resulting cocone has the required leg. The same calculation with $K\times\Delta^n$ tracks every parameter simplex, not only the vertices. For $\eta:W\to W'$, Step 1 gives $N(E_W)\to N(E_{W'})$; composition of maps of right fibrations becomes restriction of lifts, and the degreewise currying in Step 6 turns it into restriction of cocones. Thus the two maps in the naturality square agree through the constructed comparison, in every parameter degree.

source.place: Straightening naturality and explicit slice/pinch maps. Evaluation and weight-naturality calculation written here.

proof.text: Naturality in $F$ and $z$ uses the same construction with these variables retained. For $F$, form the pullback along the evaluation map $B\times\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal C)\to\mathcal C$, rather than separately for each vertex $F$. For $z$, retain the target variable of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$ and the second variable of the coherent Hom bifunctor of [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality]. Restriction of these constructions to any parameter simplex is the construction above; all face and degeneracy restrictions commute with the pullback, evaluation and currying maps. The cone/evaluation and specific Hom comparisons of [lem-coef-cone-straightening-coherent-evaluation] are coherently natural under base pullback and in $F,z$. Thus the equivalences are induced by one comparison with parameters, giving the asserted coherent naturality in $F,z$; no independent objectwise inverses are chosen. Only right fibrations, mapping spaces and functor categories were used, so no colimit in $\mathcal C$ was required. If $W$ is empty, $K$ is empty and both transformation spaces are the one-point space of maps out of an empty domain; this also treats $A=\varnothing$. All categories of fibrations and functors are formed in a universe containing $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Parameterized pullback and transport calculation, supplementing Cisinski Proposition 6.4.9; no colimit existence is used.
